$comment: THE RUSH PURSE — GitHub issue #372, docs/38-what-the-game-is.md § 2.3, and the owner's ruling of 2026-09-10 on that issue: a round is a sitting, posted whole; the server replays the chain and derives each round's purse from the previous round's hold moment. Parsed by packages/core/src/config/rushPurse.ts, which holds the schema and the arithmetic; packages/server reads it at boot and derives every purse from a replay. PROVENANCE, per the owner's 2026-09-08 standing ruling on governed data/ values: THE ONE FIGURE IN THIS FILE, unitsPerWaveOutlasted, IS AN AGENT'S PROPOSAL, APPROVED AS DRAFTED by the product owner on 2026-09-11 (DECISIONS.md § D542), and IT IS NOT MEASURED. Its schema bounds are chosen too. What is not chosen is the RULE the figure feeds: a round pays its purse on the waves it outlasted — a count read off the server's own replay at the hold moment (core sim/rush.ts#rushWavesOutlasted) — and on nothing else the run measured, so no wait, no carried count and no quotable mean can move a purse (docs/38 § 2.3: 'Nothing about the purse changes because time passed'; § D526 clause 2's rule applied to units). WHAT SPENDS IT, since GitHub issue #372's second criterion was built (DECISIONS.md § D1295): a rebuild between rounds. A round after the first may carry the tiers bought before it, as data/price-schedule.json row ids of the rush menu that packages/core/src/config/rushRebuild.ts holds (Doors, Control and Car size at every level, Tenants at the first; Shafts and Machines are refused because they need the viewer's commissioning code, and Tenants 2 and 3 because they change who arrives). The server prices them from its own copy of the schedule, now read by packages/core/src/config/priceSchedule.ts, takes the price from the balance the rounds before left, refuses a rebuild that balance cannot pay for, and replays the round on the tower fitted with everything the sitting has bought so far. This sentence used to say that nothing could spend the purse because the code that turns a kit into a building was the viewer's and the server may not import it; DECISIONS.md § D606 recorded the shapes that could close that gap, and § D1295 took the first of them for numbers only: the price reader and the copy-free half of the shop moved into core, and the shop's names and sentences did not. So the server derives and publishes each round's purse, and what each round's rebuild spent from it; packages/server/src/leaderboard/rushSitting.ts says how.
note: CHOSEN: 2 units a wave outlasted, the dispatcher tier's typical price in data/price-schedule.json. At that rate a round that outlasts five waves pays 10 units — about one equipment-tier change (typical 9) — and a round that outlasts ten pays 20, about one building-tier change (typical 20), which is docs/38 § 2.3's 'a player who lasts longer has more to rebuild with' as a ladder a player can read. MEASURED, and only as context for the choice rather than as its derivation: the waves a round outlasts under collective on each shipped tower as built — garden-apartments 6, midtown-office 9, crown-hotel 11, chancery-house 15, secure-tower 15, st-jude-hospital 16, mixed-use-high-rise 25, and all 30 on vertical-city and burj-class-reference, which never cross the line (RUSH_SITTING_COST_OUT=/tmp/rush-sitting-cost.md npx vitest run --project server packages/server/src/leaderboard/rushSitting.cost.test.ts, 2026-09-11). So a first round pays 12 to 50 units at this figure, and the smallest shipped tower's first round buys roughly one equipment-tier change. The purse is a balance within the sitting: it opens at whatever the listed top-up sinks bought (nothing on the standard board), each round pays into it, and it is spent by a rebuild between rounds, which takes its price before the round it opens plays (DECISIONS.md § D1295). CHOSEN, and stated because invariant 8 asks for it: the figure may be tuned over 1–20 units; 1 is the least a wave can pay and still be a purse, and 20 would let one wave buy a building-tier change. APPROVED AS DRAFTED by the product owner on 2026-09-11: the figure, its 1–20 schema, and the purse as a balance whose unspent units carry to the next round (DECISIONS.md § D542).
